Night paradoisis symptoms occur when you are very stressed out about something happening and you're terrified but in your dreams you don't wake up so you wake up feeling terrible feeling terrified and anxious and confused later.

Night paradosis symptoms on the other hand occur when you are freaking out over something that's probably not going to happen but instead of letting it go you wake up after an anxiety filled dream thinking about the thing that scared you thinking it might happen in real life so you're even more freaked out even though there's nothing.

Hey, can you give me some information on how construction contracts work?
Construction contracts are contracts that detail the terms and conditions for a construction project between a client and a construction company or contractor.

Can you give me an example of a construction project that might require a contract?
Certainly. In order to understand this better let’s assume that a client wants to build a house for themselves and hires “Builder A” to do the work for them.

What might that contract say?
If the contract were written it might have terms detailing:
-What is the task that Builder A will perform
-The materials that will be used
-The timeline for completion and payment
-The scope of work that needs to be completed

The contract might go on to say that Builder A is solely responsible for anything that goes wrong during the construction process. Builder A might be compensated based on a fixed fee or based on the cost of materials and labor.

If there is any dispute between the client and Builder A over the final costs of the project the client can take legal action in court.

Can I use this example to explain a situation to a five-year-old?
Yes, you can say: “A construction contract is like a promise between two people. One person might be making a house for someone else. The other person might be doing the work. A construction contract would say how much money they both need to expect, and what the work will be like.”

Can I use these bullet points as part of a legal document for this contract?
The bullet points you have mentioned could be good information to include in any contracts you make with other people. They can give people a basic understanding of what is expected in the contract.

How would the courts decide if there is a mistake in this contract?
If there is a dispute between the client and builder the client can ask the court to either side with them or rule that the builder followed their terms and conditions when completing the work. In general however courts do not generally look at documents very closely unless a person asks them to, so the court may not have enough information to rule on a construction contract if it is not included in a formal legal document.

Can these samples of construction contracts be found online freely?
Most construction contracts these days will be paper copies only unless the client pays a fee online for an electronic contract. However in some cases contracts can be found online.

Can the clauses within these construction contracts be changed by the client or have negotiations with the builder before a contract is finalised?
Normally when a contract is finalized it should contain the phrases agreed between the client and the builder that are legally binding. These are called clauses and sometimes some of them can be changed by the client.

Sometimes the final version of the contract can contain both clauses agreed between the client and builder plus other clauses added by the client or added in compliance with a legal demand from a third party.

How do I know which clauses I agreed to when signing a construction contract?
When you sign a contract the builder will usually list all the clauses in an appendix at the end. These will also contain any additional clauses agreed between the client and builder personally.

If any part of the contract goes to court and the judge states this in their decision then that decision will contain these additional clauses.

Is there anything else I should know about construction contracts?
Construction contracts can be important legal documents because they give the client a contract with the builder outlining the terms and conditions for providing money for work that will not be done according to plan.

If there is any dispute over the final costs of the project the client can take legal action in court and they will usually get a resolution that they agree with.

If the contract states that the person doing the work is a specialist in their trade that is usually good, as specialist tradespeople are more likely to provide safe work.

If the contract contains clauses saying the person doing the work is solely responsible for anything that goes wrong then this means the client could be responsible for any problems even if they didn’t invite any mistakes.

You could find samples of construction contracts online for a fee or simply ask a friend or family member if they have a contract they would be happy to send.

How many clauses should a contract have?
Most construction contracts usually contain between twelve and thirty clauses with an appendix listing any additional clauses agreed between the client and builder personally.

The exact number of clauses can depend on the client’s requirements and how much control they have over the design and work of the project.

If a contract contains too many clauses the builder may not be comfortable signing it if they don’t have all the details they need.

If it has more clauses than you think will ever be needed or want a contractor may decide not to go through with the project and it can cost the client a lot more than if the contract had a smaller number of clauses.

The client may also have more control over the design and work of the project if the contract doesn’t have enough clauses. If something goes wrong they probably won’t have much legal recourse and it will be easier to resolve if there are enough clauses in the contract.

Are there different types of construction contract?
There is more than one type of construction contract and these include:

- Commercial contract: A commercial contract covers any activity that needs a contract, whether it’s for something as small as buying food in a shop or something much bigger like buying an aircraft.
- Design and build contract: In this type of contract the builder is responsible for the design and development of the project and then builds it themselves. If any part goes wrong the builder is usually responsible too.
- Full project management contract (also called off-site management contract): A full project management contract is similar to a design and build contract but instead of building the project the contractor will work on the project from start to finish.

To understand these contracts better think about the type of job you might get done in your family home and think about how this would work if done for larger projects like building a house extension.

Do designers usually enter into contracts with builders as part of these different types?

Sometimes designers will use construction contracts to enter into contracts with builders themselves which will give them more control over how the project will be managed.

Designers have different priorities than the client or the builder, so the design phase will be focused on creating a beautiful but simple and functional concept and the build phase will focus on creating a design which meets those goals.

How do designers usually decide what their fees will be in relation to these different different types?

For large design and build projects with many different contractors involved these might not always be easy questions to answer.

There might not be enough time to just come up with a fixed fee for these projects.

Some designers might take a percentage of the total price, which would mean they would earn less if the price went up and more if it went down.
Designers might enter into a project cost-recovery model where they charge a fee only after the building work has been completed.

There might also be options where it depends more heavily on whether the customer wants a designer-managed contract where all costs are taken from the fee paid to the designer by the client and where there could be more risk for the designer with full-build contracts for large projects.

This might help you understand how these contracts might differ from other contracts you might make yourself or perhaps someone else makes for the projects you’re interested in doing by reading their individual Terms and Conditions.

Do designers normally own their own equipment like tools etc?
Designers may own their own equipment like tools and other items but usually they will not own the materials used to build the project in the normal course of building works.

They will own the creative skills used in the design but not the physical work items that are used for building the project that are not owned by those companies like steel frames or flooring companies.

It depends more on the complexity and scale of each project.

If the project plan includes creating custom components then their skills and equipment may be all they need and need not to purchase third-party equipment like engineers might use when designing and managing an infrastructure project would require the purchase of site equipment like drilling rigs.

Designers usually will know their trade very well and know where materials can be found locally in the right sizes if not as the designers design requests some from third-party companies which themselves might use local suppliers.

They may have partnerships with companies which offer steel frames for example where the designer makes some custom components.

What does a full project management contract look like in legal terms?
A full project management contract is an appropriate form of contract when there is a degree of budget, time, and risk involvement from the client which doesn’t fit into any of the standard forms of contracts that typically exist.

These types of contracts are usually used when the client wants more control over who works on the project, the way the project is managed and the budget for the project.

Under a full project management contract it could be expected that the client would provide all resources such as staff, materials and equipment that are required for the project and will manage each step of the project themselves.

When the client chooses a full project management contract rather than typical commercial contracts they are usually committing themselves to many responsibilities that go beyond those usually found in commercial contracts and in almost all construction projects.

These responsibilities usually vary depending on the type of project and industry.

Full project management contracts usually come complete with standard clauses from a contract law perspective and will contain standard forms from a risk control perspective.

For example you will likely see standard form conditions which outlines if and how each party will indemnify each other against some risks which can include the risks of delays or non-completion of the project.

Full project management contracts sometimes have performance bonds and termination fees which means if there is any issues affecting the performance of the project these could result in significant financial losses to the client which could possibly lead to lawyers being involved.

-More control for the client over the project management and more freedom and expertise for the designer
-Distraction from the project to focus other work or allow time

Here follow some recommendations for how much and what type of weight you'd use depending on your goals and equipment.

Here are a few reasons why it could benefit your strength training goals to vary how much weight used for each weightlift:

They allow muscles to adapt more easily because each repetition requires slightly different stress.

Each weight may also use slightly different muscle fibers which results in slightly different adaptations.

This ensures a greater chance of muscles being over the long term stronger on the movements you want them to be.

It is important to note here that the above does not mean to use as much weight as possible with each move or attempt as this can have negative consequences.

With very heavy weight the muscles become damaged which can last for a long time or trigger inflammation and soreness.

In addition the possibility of muscle imbalances developing due to which muscle groups are used more heavily can also increase the risk of failure and the development of injury.

Thus the guidelines above only recommend the use of weights which allow muscles to adapt and become stronger over time on an individual repetition basis.

Can you explain the term "micro-tears"?
@@@ The term "micro-tears" might refer to microscopic tears or damage to the cells of the muscles and/or tendons during weightlifting exercises.

These tears usually occur when the muscle fibers are stretched or stretched beyond their repair capacity due to the continuous stress applied to them during weightlifting.

For example imagine placing a heavy book on your desk.

If you keep placing and removing the book from the vicinity of your desk for an extended period of time without giving the book enough space to move around and come in contact only with parts of the book that need attention such as the most fragile and stressed areas, eventually your desk will wear out or break due to constantly putting pressure on the most vulnerable parts.

The same goes for the muscles in your body.

If you repeatedly apply high-impact stress to the muscles while weightlifting despite knowing they are capable of handling it on an individual level without causing damage beyond the scope of what may be reasonable in size or possibility in the future, micro-tears can occur when trying to train with heavy weight and/or an intense amount of reps and sets.

This puts immense stress on the muscles and tendons thus causing damage when there isn't a clear path forward for how they can withstand such a pressure.

It also explains why weightlifters often wear protective gear such as gloves whenever possible as well as pads for their weights.

This gear provides a sanctuary for the hands and weights such that when applied the impact can only reach these areas that are specifically designed to take the stress.

This may not always be possible though and protective gear may only partially counteract the negative impact and can often only partially reduce or prevent micro-tears from occurring.

There is a fine line between using protective gear to reduce the risk of micro-tears when it may not be necessary as well as using gear that may increase micro-tears somewhat unnecessarily.

Thus it can become a matter of finding what level of protection, if any is correct for an individual lifter while being mindful not to put undue stress on the hands or weights preventing their ability to perform with correct technique.

So as you can see the micro-tears theory isn't perfect yet we know quite well how muscle and/or tendin injuries typically develop as a result of unpreventable micro-tears getting out of proportion.

It would be beneficial to research further ways that weightlifting exercises may not only reduce micro-tears but also to prevent them from occurring in the first place while training.

As a side note micro-tears typically cause a loss of full strength or muscle tone so someone may feel fine at first but experience reduced muscle strength in the long run.

When training to lift more weights and/or lift heavier weights one should expect to feel some micro-tears which may be manageable during training when preventing micro-tears is generally more beneficial even if it does require using some protective gear.

The term "micro-tear" doesn't make sense without mentioning the other term "myositis ossificans", can you explain the difference here as well?
@@@ In terms of the differences between micro-tears and myositis ossificans, the term "micro-tear" tends to describe damaged muscle fibers caused by over-stressing the muscles due to weightlifting.

In contrast myositis ossificans describes a rare but serious condition caused by excessive calcification and muscle thickening occurring as a result of long-standing problems within muscles such as myositis and tendonitis or chronic infections causing damage to the tissues around them and resulting in a build-up of calcium deposits which may progress to the formation of bone within the muscle tissue.

The calcium deposits commonly occur within the muscle fibers causing the muscle to stiffen further and making it harder for the muscles to become flexible again.

Causes
The two conditions mentioned above can generally occur if the muscles are repeatedly over-stressed.

Symptoms
In terms of symptoms there can be significant differences between the two conditions.

For micro-tears soreness and sometimes even pain in the muscle or tendons may occur in the affected area which may progress gradually.

With myositis ossificans the symptoms may begin with muscle pain but may become severe and disabling if left untreated causing difficulties standing and walking and in extreme cases death following a breakdown within muscles and/or tendons which may have been poorly managed despite appropriate treatment.

Risk factors there are several other risk factors for both conditions but generally they do not overlap significantly.

Myositis can arise from any cause that causes long-standing problems in muscles.
Tennis elbow, repetitive strain injuries to the hand and a weakening hand from holding a telephone for an extended period are some examples.

Tendonitis occurs when the tendons connecting muscles become inflamed due to constant strain.

Athlete's Bunion, Tennis Elbow and Carpal-Tenosin Tunnel Inflammation which causes long-standing problems with the wrist and finger tendons can also result in problems with the small bones (Bony projections at the base of the big and small toes)

Conclusion
Weightlifting is a very beneficial physical activity however it is important to recognize the risks associated with it.

To prevent micro-tears caused by improper technique weights should not be too heavy and an essential focus should be placing the proper amount of emphasis on using proper technique.

Myositis ossificans may be prevented through early diagnosis and correct treatment.

Weightlifters should take precautions regarding how much weight they are lifting so as not to put excess stress on their muscles and take breaks when necessary.
As well exercises that may aggravate the condition such as heavy weights or prolonged use of the wrist and finger should be avoided.

Can you tell me more about myositis?
@@@ In general myositis refers to a long-standing condition that develops within muscles and the muscles that connect and relate to the bones within the body causing them to weaken over time.

Myositis can be categorized as inflammatory or non-inflammatory depending on the type of cell involved within the muscle fibers.

Inflammation may involve either the myocytes or the extra cellular elements such as the fibroblasts or macrophages which all play a role within the formation of new muscle fibers within muscles.

Myositis can be defined by abnormal accumulation and organization of calcium within the cell membranes (endoplasmic reticulums or ERs), within the nucleus and/or cytoplasm of muscle fibers although the type and severity of calcium build-up is dependent on exactly which type of muscle cells are involved within the condition.

Causes
Myositis has several possible causes although many researchers still hold that there is not one universal cause.

Some common conditions that can increase the risk of myositis include vitamin and mineral deficiencies such as iron, copper, or magnesium, autoimmune diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus or Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus and disorders affecting bone growth such as osteomalacia and chronic kidney disease which can make muscles and bones less able to repair themselves and heal.

Other conditions such as infections, toxins and exposure to radiation may contribute to the development of myositis.

Additionally it can be linked to psychological issues including anxiety and depression.

Symptoms
The symptoms of myositis depend on which cells are impacted by the condition although most will include pain and weakness in muscles.

There may also be other symptoms depending on how severe the condition is such as fatigue and muscle

Article:

Title: A Step-by-Step Guide to Updating Your Living Space with Clean and Modern Furniture

Introduction

Living spaces can transform with just a little bit of sprucing up. One area to consider is furniture and decor for your home. It’s never too early or too late to give your living space a modern upgrade with fresh furniture and an overhauling color palette and décor elements. With easy steps and some helpful suggestions, anyone can make their living space feel modern, bright and inviting.

Step One: Get rid of old, dirty furniture

One of the best places to start your living room overhaul is by removing anything that hasn’t seen significant maintenance in the last six months. That means old sheets on your bed from the holidays or outdated pillows from before Hurricane Matthew devastated your hometown in 2016. If your furniture still has visible wear and tear or is more than ten years old, it may be time for a new purchase.

Step Two: Remove carpeting

For homes with hardwood, laminate, or tile flooring, removing carpet can create an open and airy feel in the room. Alternatively, if you prefer carpeted surfaces, consider adding colorful area rugs to cover the bare flooring. Add an accent wall in a bold color or pattern and pair it back with neutral-colored wall paint for a modern look.

Step Three: Paint or stain wood surfaces

A fresh coat of paint and a wood-stain job can completely transform the look of your living space. Painting adds both sophistication and a contemporary feel to your home with an easy and cost-effective option. Alternatively, consider staining your wood furniture, which provides a rich, natural look for your living room furniture. Both options are suitable for homeowners with limited painting experience.

Step Four: Update lighting fixtures

Upgrading your lighting fixtures will significantly impact the visual ambiance of your living space. Aim for fixtures made of modern materials such as metal, glass, or ceramic to tie in with the contemporary style. Choose a single light source such as a pendant lamp or floor lamp, rather than an abundance of table lamps or floor lamps to maintain a clean and unified look.

Conclusion

It is essential to remember that updating your furniture and décor doesn’t have to be an expensive investment. With just a little effort and the right combination of furniture, paint colors and décor elements, you can give your living space a fresh and modern look.

@@@ Rephrase:  While it would certainly be impossible to summarize the internet’s entire history in just one short sentence, one key aspect of internet history that stands out to me is the invention of Hypertext in the 1960s by Sir Tim Berners-Lee.

This invention was an enormous turning point in internet history as it allowed for the creation of hyperlinks and hypermedia, which revolutionized how content would be accessed and disseminated in the future.

The key distinction between hypertext and traditional text-based communications was the linking of independent pieces of information (called "nodes") rather than traditional links linking to a particular body of text (called a "link"). In hypertext, these linked pieces of information were called "links", each carrying its own identifier or "URI".

This allowed for a much more fluid and interactive experience for users browsing the web as they could easily move from one node to another by clicking on the links between them.

Rather than being limited to traditional media such as printed paper or oral presentations in lecture halls, hypertext enabled the internet to become a comprehensive open-access knowledge space. This space was made possible by computers and internet connectivity which allowed for the seamless collaboration and dissemination of information between disparate nodes.

Additionally this innovation allowed for another key invention in the design and development of the World Wide Web which was the creation of hypermedia in Hypertext at the time.

The World Wide Web represents the ultimate achievement of hypertext design principles as it has enabled the distribution of information using web-pages which can be stored on a user's computer hard-drive (called the "Client/Computer"), can be browsed and retrieved through standard web-browsers on desktop or mobile devices connected to the Internet (called the "Server/Network"), and which can contain all sorts of content including images, html markup and external documentation from other servers located on the web.

The structure and functioning of web-pages relies heavily on the use of hyperlinks to connect content between pages and enable navigation within a web-domain. These hyperlinks link to other web-pages (called "hyperlinks" or "href's"), which contain more structured content with their own sub-sections or elements such as headings or paragraphs.

This type of structured content can themselves link to other web-pages (called "anchor-elements") in different languages, further linking together content throughout the entire web-domain.

This hierarchical organization of pages and content based on hyperlinks provides a method of organizing and providing access to large amounts of interconnected data which does not depend on the traditional print or other physical media utilized for distribution.

As hypertext allowed content to be accessed and organized hierarchically according to its relevance and relationship with other nodes (called "path-links"), hypertext design principles allowed for the development of the concept of "topic models" which are now widely used for natural language processing tasks to gain insight into text documents containing text of varied complexity within large collections of documents where the relationships among these documents are unknown in advance.

The topic model is based on features which relate to the structure and presentation of the document corpus and the text of each document's topic is calculated as a linear combination of these document-feature features extracted from the corpus of documents.

This linear combination of text features is then used to predict or classify the topic within a particular document, text, speech or other such multivariate data set.

What is hypertext What is hypertext

hypertext is a web technology that uses links to other web pages and documents.

In terms of history

Sir Tim Berners-Lee invented Hypertext in 1989 to store and share information about his research in the Department of Technology at the University of Cern in Switzerland.

At the time Berners-Lee was working on a project called the "WorldWideWeb" which allows users to access and share information electronically. However at the time Berners-Lee did not have a clear idea of how something called "hyperlinks"

Berners-Lee was looking into ways to organize text so he could easily find related information when working on his job at the university.

he observed that the way text was displayed on screen made it difficult to easily move between different parts of the text.

He was also concerned that links between different parts of a document were indirect rather than immediate.

This led him to create the Hypertext transfer protocol HTTP in 1989.

This protocol allowed web servers to send links or hyperlinks to web clients directly from one web page to another rather than requiring the user to click on a hyperlink in the original text-based document.

Berners-Lee also created the World Wide Web standard HTML (Hyper Text Markup Language) in the same year.

This standard allowed web pages to be created and organized using the Hypertext tags which allowed users to easily include text, images and other types of content in a structured and hierarchical manner,

Berners-Lee designed the Hypertext transfer protocol to make it easy for web servers to send hyperlinks directly to web clients.

Berners-Lee believed it was important for web servers to be able to send hyperlinks to their clients in clear text so the web server web server could send hyperlinks to the client directly through HTTP protocol instead of requiring the user to click on a text-based hyperlink contained within the original web page itself.

Berners-Lee understood that it

was important for web clients to be able to easily determine the destination web page.

In addition he wanted web clients to have the option of opening the intended web page in their browser without the server sending them as clear text the address and path of the link they wanted to open.

so he incorporated support for the HTTP Referer HTTP header in Berners-Lee’s original Hypertext Transfer Protocol in 1989.

univ.

Prefix or CIIR) as the identifier for the referring web server.

Berners-Lee believed it important to allow both absolute and relative URLs in web pages to be included in the Referer header.

In this task you will be given a list of integers. You should remove any integer that is not prime. A prime integer is an integer that is only divisible by '1' and itself. The output should be the list of prime integers, sorted in ascending order.

[509, 590, 261, 541]

Okay, let's go through this step by step:

1. We're told we'll get a list of integers.
2. We know what "prime" means: A prime integer is an integer that has no positive divisors other than '1' and itself.
3. So we need to extract those integers which aren't divisible by anything except '1'.

What is the algorithm then, step by step by step explanation?
Let's go through the steps:

Step 1:
We will receive an integer list, which contains at least one integer.

Step 2:
First, we'll filter out the integers that aren't prime. To do this, we can go through each integer in the list individually.

Step 3:
If the integer isn't divisible by anything other than '1' then it's a prime integer.

Step 4:
Finally, we'll sort the prime integers in ascending order.

Here's a Python code implementation of the solution:

```python
def is_prime(n):
    if n < 2:
        return False
    for i in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1):
        if n % i == 0:
            return False
    return True

numbers = [509, 590, 261, 541]
prime_numbers = [num for num in numbers if is_prime(num)]

prime_numbers.sort()

print(prime_numbers)
```

So you would output:

```
[509, 541]
```

The step-by-step explanation above shows how this task involves determining if each integer is prime or not and then selecting only those primes. The prime numbers are then sorted in ascending order.

Can you explain the difference between supervised and unsupervised learning in machine learning?
Yes, in machine learning there are two main types of learning: supervised learning and unsupervised learning. 

Supervised Learning:
In supervised learning, the machine learning algorithm is trained on a labeled data set. This means that each data point in the set has an associated label or target value that the algorithm tries to predict. The algorithm is trained on the input data and the corresponding target values, and it learns to map the input data to the target values. Once the algorithm is trained, it can be used to predict the target values for new, unseen data points. Examples of supervised learning include classification (where the target value is a categorical variable) and regression (where the target value is a continuous numerical value).

Unsupervised Learning:
In unsupervised learning, the machine learning algorithm is not given labeled data to train on. Instead, the algorithm tries to discover patterns and relationships in the data without any prior knowledge of what the correct outcomes should be. The goal of unsupervised learning is often to cluster data points together based on their similarity, but it can also be used for other types of analysis. Examples of unsupervised learning include clustering (where the goal is to group similar data points together) and anomaly detection (where the goal is to identify data points that are significantly different from the rest of the dataset).

解释一下美国宪法里要求人们宣誓效忠的原因
这个问题的答案因人而异，但是在美国和其他大陆上，在加入军队前签署的誓词要求公民代表统治阶级来保卫国家是一件再正常不过的事情。当他们加入军队的时候，他们需要代表军队，宣誓效忠，这也是对自由权的一种保护。这正是美国宪法要求士兵宣誓的主要原因。在加入政府（例如一个议会议员、州长或总统）的时候，加入者也需要宣誓效忠。
在英国，与美国的誓言有所不同。当那些通过选举产生政府官员的时候，这些官员通常需要签署一份放弃对国王的臣服和对法律的尊重的声明。官员们也签署了一份放弃他们在这个国家所拥有的权力并且把他们移交给“尊贵的议会”的声明。议会可以全部或部分修改这些宣言。这种对一个新政府的宣言称为“政府同意宣言”。在英国和美国的政府同意宣言的目的，主要起着保护立法权的作用。因为立法权应该受法律的限制，所以这种放弃对国王和法律的尊重的规定保护了立法权免受国家至上或个人意志的威胁。

英美的案例是否说明如果总统和国会议员的宣誓内容不一样怎么办？
这个问题要看情况来定，不同的承诺是建立在一个基础之上的。如果基础不同，誓言也就失去了意义。比如，当华盛顿当选为美国第一任总统的时候，他需要签署放弃他对国家的统治，并且放弃他对司法和宪法的解释和适用的声明。这个声明的目的是要确立“国会为政府的最高行政领导机关”的原则。华盛顿总统签署的宣言就是美国政府同意宣言的基础，从而确保了国家最高行政权力（总统）和立法权力（国会）之间的平衡。
但是在英美两国政府同意宣言中并不规定总统对法律的解释和适用的权力是对或否。当两个人签署了政府同意宣言，他们就承认了国会有对国家的法律做出最终解释和决定的权力，这是两种最完全不同的形式，因而不能用同一个基础去解释或评价这两种形式。但是这种互相承认的效果表明了他们对立法权的尊崇和对另一个政府（国会）的承认。

The Evolution and Legacy of Mean Girls

To understand ‘Mean Girls,’ it is crucial to go back to its origins, the book of equal measure of fiction and cautionary tale written by actress-turned-author Gigi Goode in the mid-1990s (published in 2000). Perhaps most importantly, ‘Mean Girls’ serves as an emblematic reminder of the innocence and the complexities that characterize our pre-teen years or adolescence. In many ways it’s the perfect window into our childhood, offering us glimpses into the mindsets and challenges that we’ll grapple with as teenagers.

How is "I will make this clear later." said in Czech?
In Czech, you'd say "Přijde ti to ještě pozděj." Here's a simple explanation:

"Přijde" means "I will come" or "I will arrive", it's a future form of verb indicating a probable future event.
"ti" means "to you", it's referring to the person who will come later.
"ještě" means "later", it's used to introduce an upcoming event or situation.
"Pozděj" means "soon", it means the future event will happen soon.

So when you put it all together, "Přijde ti to ještě pozděj." means "I will come to you later." It's a polite way to ask someone for help or attention a little later.

Stars come in different sizes and shapes and can be categorized according to their temperature. The most massive stars burn through their fuel at a much faster speed than the sun on Earth, which produces gamma-rays with energies higher than that of the Higgs boson that is heavier than any known particle.

As the star consumes its fuel and heats up, it generates more energy through a process called nuclear fusion, in which protons from the core combine to form heavier elements like helium and then heavier ones like carbon and oxygen. The fusion reaction of four hydrogen nuclei (protons) with a single helium nucleus occurs at the center of most stars.

The temperature and pressure in the core increase as the fusion reactions proceed, and the star begins to take shape with a spherical shape and a luminous surface, known as the photosphere. The gravitational force of the sun attracts the gas and dust within its visible envelope, giving rise to the sun's light and heat.

However, it is the core of the most massive stars that undergoes an even more intense fusion process known as neutron degenerate fusion, in which two protons combine to form a neutron-star nucleus consisting of one neutron and no protons. This reaction further generates energy until the core becomes dense and hot enough that it collapses under its own weight, forming a black hole, or singularity if this process continues infinitely.

As the core collapses further, the pressure and temperature reach critical levels and nuclear reactions stop due to the lack of fuel (hydrogen). The star then expands into a red giant and begins to cool through a process called helium-shell fusion, in which the core of the star burns through the outer layers of hydrogen to fuse helium atoms together until the core contains mostly helium. When this occurs, the star contracts in shape and starts rotating faster.

If it is no longer able to fuse helium atoms together, the star undergoes a flash of nuclear fusion known as a core-collapse supernova explosion, which releases an incredibly powerful burst of energy in the form of light and radiation that can be observed from Earth.

Stars can also take on other shapes and sizes depending on their composition and evolution. Planetary nebulae and later the formation of planets within a star's core is thought to have formed through the accumulation of dense, angularly shaped debris as suggested by the similarity between planetary nebulae and the shapes and features of newly formed planets orbiting low-mass stars.

And even cooler and fainter stars can only shine for brief intervals as their cores gradually lose gravitational support and come to rest within a dense, hot, and narrow core called the white dwarf. These objects have sufficient density and temperature for the electron degeneracy pressure to overcome the force of repulsion between the negatively charged electrons and remain stable in their current configuration.

Moving inside

the innermost layer is the eyelids that protect the eye from debris and facial expression.

Can you provide me with further details about the process of data mining and its applications in various fields? Could you also expand on the "relevance sampling" approach employed in data mining?
Sure, I can definitely help with that!
1. What is data mining?
   
Data mining is a field that involves the process of discovering patterns and relationships in large datasets. It uses various techniques like statistical analysis, machine learning, and data visualization to identify interesting information that can be useful for decision-making, customer segmentation, or predicting future trends.

2. Applications of data mining

The applications of data mining are very diverse and wide-ranging. It has applications in:
- Business: to improve customer orientation and predictive modeling to optimize inventory levels and improve sales processes.
- Healthcare: identifying patients who are at high risk for certain diseases to enable preventive care, as well as to develop new treatments.
- Finance: detecting credit card fraud or fraud in financial transactions.
- Education: personalized learning.
- Internet and e-commerce: spam filtering and user behavior analysis.

3. Relevant sampling techniques

In data mining, one common technique is relevance sampling. In this approach, a small subset of all the data is selected and viewed in order to predict the outcome of the sampling. A subset is selected based on various criteria like popularity, timeliness or relevance, which makes it a predictive sampling technique. Another popular sampling technique is random sampling.

Can you elaborate on relevance sampling in data mining?
Relevance sampling is a type of predictive sampling used in data mining. The goal of relevance sampling is to select a subset of the data that most closely reflects the interest and purpose of the analyst or user who will interpret the results of the analysis. This technique reduces the amount of irrelevant or noise in the data and helps focus the analysis on the relevant information.

To select the relevant subset of data for analysis using relevance sampling, several techniques can be applied:

1. Ranking: The dataset can be ranked based on how relevant it is to the user's query. This can be determined by assigning numerical values to each record, where higher values indicate greater relevance.

2. Time-sensitive ordering: Choose data based on when they were updated or when the query was last seen by the data mining algorithm.

3. Personalized ranking: Assign numerical values to each record based on how closely it matches the user's query.

4. Time-based sampling: Select data at specific times throughout the day or week.

The relevance of each record in the dataset is an important consideration in relevance sampling because it helps to ensure that relevant information that can answer the user's query or inform decision-making is included in the analysis.

Are there any limitations or challenges in using relevance sampling technique in data mining?
Yes, relevance sampling has some limitations and challenges:

1. Sample size: Selecting a sample that is representative enough of the population can be tricky and the right quantity and quality of data is crucial.

2. Over-reliance: There is a risk of relying too heavily on the relevance sampling method for data exploration and decision-making.

3. Selection bias: There is a possibility of introducing a selection bias if different criteria are used to select the relevant subset in the data mining process.

4. Unforeseen consequences: Selecting the relevant subset can have unforeseen consequences that may not have been anticipated, which could have negative consequences.

Overall relevance sampling is a useful technique for data mining when certain criteria need to be upheld such as timeliness or popularity of data records.

Can you give me an example scenario where relevance sampling would be particularly useful in data mining?
Sure! Let's say a social media company wants to understand what types of content their users engage with the most. A common way they could explore this information would be to perform a traditional statistical analysis on the raw data gathered over an entire period of time. However, this could be error-prone and time-consuming in an application where the analysis needs to happen frequently.

In this case relevance sampling could be a more effective method to analyze the data quickly and efficiently, and get insights into what types of topics or themes tend to appear more frequently than others in their user population. This information could then be utilized by the social media team to develop strategies for promoting content that will be most likely to drive engagement and attract new users.

How does data mining differ from traditional statistical analysis in gathering and analyzing large datasets? Can relevance sampling applied specifically to these types of datasets too?
Data mining and traditional statistical analysis share some similarities in gathering and analyzing large datasets, but they also have some key differences. In traditional statistical analysis:

* Analysis is generally based on some pre-defined model or equation that can include both quantitative and qualitative variables

* Data is usually arranged in rows and doesn't have any structure or order

Data mining, on the other hand, uses techniques like association rule mining to explore and explore relationships between different variables within the data and isn't typically as focused on developing mathematical models.

As for relevance sampling,

* It can also explore relationships between variables within the data

However relevance sampling isn't typically built around developing mathematical models.

So the way relevance sampling is applied specifically to datasets depends on certain conditions (like the time and rate at which data changes), making it a useful additional tool when combined with other data mining techniques like association rule mining or statistical analysis.

2. Online Data Mining Handbook by Michael J. Ray - this book provides a comprehensive guide to data mining and presents relevant examples from different domains.

3. Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow by Aurélien Géron - this book is a comprehensive guide for both beginners and advanced learners interested in machine learning using Python libraries. 
4. Data Mining Solutions by Paul D. Kianidou - this book contains data mining algorithms and practical applications examples using python libraries such as pandas, numpy, and scikit-learn.

I hope these resources will help you gain a good understanding of data mining techniques as well as relevance sampling. Good luck!

Can you tell me more about how to prepare datasets for data mining and explain the importance of data cleaning in this process?
Sure thing! Data cleaning is an important part of preparing data for data mining purposes. In data mining algorithms, there may be technical or spelling errors in the data, inconsistencies in the data that need to be addressed before analysis can proceed, missing data that needs to be dealt with correctly.

In general data cleaning involves several tasks:

1. Data transformation: This involves converting some attributes or values of data into units that measure the data.

2. Handling missing data: Missing data need to be handled properly in data mining. There are several techniques to fill missing data such as imputation methods like mean, median or mode imputation, regression imputation and removal.

3. Removing outliers: Outliers are extreme data points that may skew statistical results. To avoid this type of problems in data mining need to remove the outliers.

Data cleaning in data mining is important because:

1. To make accurate predictions: Any errors in the data can affect the accuracy of the data mining algorithm.

2. To avoid statistical loss: Statistical loss occurs when data quality is poor. Incorrect results can occur when statistical methods are used.

3. To ensure the scalability and generalizability of results: Poor quality data can reduce the ability of data mining models to generalize and can lead to poor predictive performance.

I hope this helps! Let me know if you have any more questions about this.

Great! Can you also explain the difference between supervised and unsupervised learning in data mining?
Of course! In data mining, supervised and unsupervised learning are two common approaches used to extract knowledge from data.

Supervised learning involves using labeled data to train a machine learning model to make predictions on new, unlabeled data. For example, in a spam email detection problem, we might have a labeled dataset consisting of email spam and non-spam examples, and the goal would be to train a machine learning model to predict whether new emails are spam or not.

Unsupervised learning on the other hand, involves finding patterns or structure in unlabeled data. For example, clustering problems involve grouping similar data points together based on their attributes. Anomaly detection is the problem where we look for data points that are significantly different from other data in the dataset.

The main difference between supervised and unsupervised learning lies in the way the model is trained:

Supervised learning requires labeled data and it learns to predict an output for new input. On the other hand, unsupervised learning doesn't require labels and it finds patterns or structures in data without any explicit feedback on the correctness of the output.

Both supervised and unsupervised learning have many real-world applications in data mining and other fields such as computer vision and natural language processing.

My baby isn't sleeping well lately due to loud noises like cart horns and trucks passing near her window by her daycare. Is there anything I can do at home to help her sleep better?
Hi there!

The short answer is “yes” there are several things that you can do at home to help reduce her exposure to loud noises.

## Turn on music

Music can help reduce anxiety and stress and promote peaceful sleep in your little one.

Playing some familiar soothing music can really help your little one to relax and sleep better.

When your child is young--

For newborns and very first few months of life, soothing music or white noise can really help.

For a baby who is between 3 and 12 months of age--

Music has the biggest effect when breastfeeding or while nursing or when your child is very young and tired.

### Examples of music that work well --

Lots of different kinds of music work really well.

Blues and some jazz music may not work as well because they are typically very loud and very strong for young children.

Kids' tv programs tend to have lower decibels compared with music recordings. So if your child is exposed to kids’ tv pretty regularly she may sleep better if she is in a lower decibel music/play list environment.

Video games also tend to have lower decibels compared with many music recordings.

So maybe her play-list includes some favorite video game music as well!

## Cuddle/Read Aloud

Sometimes just being close to your child can help them fall asleep and reduce the amount of noisy wake-ups and night-cries.

### What to read-aloud to your child--

Stories, books and picture books can all be very helpful in teaching your child about the world and helping him develop a love of reading.

Poetry, especially children’s poetry can also help children feel calm and relaxed.

Remember to read your child some stories and rhymes at the right level of difficulty.

## Make the room comfortable

Try these steps to help create a comfortable night’s sleep for your little one.

Make the space around her feel calm and nice.

Put her bedtime routines in place so she feel ready to sleep when she is ready.

Consider--

Using comforter and blanket colors that are calming and soothing.
Keeping the space fairly dark.

To light up the space without creating distractions around the room try

Using a variety of lights such as a night light and table lamps inside the room.

Avoiding bright screens and videos and violent TV shows/ratings.

Avoiding loud videos/music outside of her bedtime routine.

A baby girl loves to play in water. She likes to swim or play in water for a little while before bedtime.

There is some evidence showing that being in the water right before sleep can actually help childrensleep better.

So if your little girl is sleeping in a crib try putting her in some water right before sleep or right after wake-up.

Have some water in her reach (usually around 10 inches from her face).

## Use white noise machines

White noise machines work really well for reducing exposure to annoying sounds in the environment.

### Which type should you get--

White noise machines work best for reducing sounds with a lot of different frequencies separated by no more than a few cents.

They need to have a very low level of distortion such asHissing,saw-tooth and crackling sounds.

The machine should be very quiet so you don’t even notice it is working.

It should also be adjustable so you can pick the setting with the lowest amount of distortion and noise for your little one.

## Reduce room temperature

Too hot a room can make it harder for babies to fall asleep and sleep better.

Try these steps to help your little one sleep better and stay sleep-ready through the day.

Keep the room at a comfortable temperature of around 96-98 degrees Fahrenheit (about the same as your bedroom temperature).

### Methods--

The best ways to reduce the risk of sick leave for both you and your spouse’s coworkers are--

Making use of A/C:air-conditioning.

Avoid using heat-generating things like fires/geothermal energy/etc in the house.

Have a generator to use if power goes out and you need to keep your lights on so you don’t get sick leave from losing your power for being out in the dark and without heat/fan.

Also keep a hand-crank radio or battery-powered radio in case power goes out so you can listen to baby’s doctor’s appointments and other health related events.

## Encourage your child to sleep through the night

Some kids sleep through the night by around age 6 months but most kids take at least a year.

Your child may sleep longer due to her developmental level.

It may take several months of consistent developmental strategies to prepare your little one for the sleep milestones you are eager to reach.

## How can I get more help?

There are a variety of resources that may be helpful for your situation--

Parents of Young Children

Parents of School-Aged Children

Infant and Toddler Sleep

If these other resources aren’t helpful for your situation please share your most recent Gravatar message here and we will get back to you as soon as possible.

Thanks!

 Me: What is your definition of “size”? Is Earth bigger than the sun?

So from a great distance it takes about the same amount of effort to get around Earth as it does to get around the sun or Alpha Centauri A and B.

My personal favorite analogy is if you were standing on Earth and looked up at the night sky and saw the constellation Orion.
